stories.title: The Library Is Closed. Feel Free to Come In.
stories.label: people
stories.summary: A small town library has found a clever way to serve its community around the clock. Even when no staff are there, residents can use a special access system to let themselves in to read, work, or just get out of the weather. It's especially helpful in rural areas where the library might be the only free indoor gathering spot for miles. People are using the quiet after-hours time to study, meet up, or simply find a warm, welcoming space. It's a simple idea making a real difference in daily life.
stories.why_good: A real, already-running program that expands free public access to community space, especially helpful for rural residents with few other options.

stories.title: ESA's New Sentinel 3C Satellite Makes its Debut with Sumptuous Images of Italy and the Arctic
stories.label: space
stories.summary: A brand-new European satellite called Sentinel 3C just sent back its very first pictures of Earth, and they are stunning. The images show Italy's coastline, the Canadian Arctic, and the Caribbean in rich, true-to-life color. This satellite will help scientists track oceans, land, and ice from space for years to come, giving us better tools to understand our changing planet. It's a quiet little triumph of teamwork and engineering, already paying off just two weeks after launch.
stories.why_good: A real, completed space mission milestone that benefits environmental science and happened this week, with no political angle.

stories.title: Inches Below the Forest Floor, Archeologists in Germany Unearthed a Roman Temple to the War God
stories.label: science
stories.summary: Archeologists digging along an old Roman frontier line near Frankfurt, Germany, just uncovered the floorplans of an ancient temple, a military camp, and a craft center. The whole complex had been hiding only inches beneath the forest floor for nearly two thousand years. It's a rare and detailed window into daily Roman life on the empire's edge, found almost by accident. Finds like this help historians piece together how soldiers, craftspeople, and worshippers actually lived side by side. It's the kind of discovery that makes the past feel suddenly close.
stories.why_good: A genuine, completed archeological discovery that expands human knowledge with no downside or controversy.
